title: A failed write records why it failed
outcome: A queued entry whose flush failed carries the reason, so 'the backoff is spent' and 'this can never succeed' stop being the same value. Nothing observable changes yet; this is what makes the queue serialisable without losing a distinction.
acceptanceCriteria: A pending entry carries the last failure's code, reason and HTTP status, and nothing else from the error — no human-facing message or detail, which move with copy and translation.
The failure recorded is the one the flush already reports, taken from the same place that currently decides the backoff, so there is no second source for what went wrong.
An entry that has never failed carries no error at all, rather than a placeholder standing in for one.
A later successful flush of the same entry leaves no stale error behind.
Existing derivations are untouched: the sync indicator, the per-row failure marker and the unconfirmed-set dialog read exactly what they read today, so this slice changes no screen.
